variants.headline: Business plan abandoned before opening
variants.sub: The planned {business} will not open: {founder} has given up the plan.
variants.body:
The founder {founder} has abandoned the plan for {business} before opening. The reason given is that {why}. The builder keeps what it was paid, and any grant is owed back. For {target}, the result raises a direct question about responsibility before an enterprise can begin operating.

A terminated plan can retain financial consequences. The builder keeps sums already paid, and any grant remains repayable. Commercial readers should distinguish the end of the intended business from the clearing of its commitments; abandoning the proposal does not amount to a full reversal of the transactions around it.

The responsibility of {target} should be considered through the abandoned plan and its remaining obligations. The outcome is not an operating company's failure, but the end of a proposal before opening. Reliable assessment begins with particulars rather than a politically convenient assumption.
